Sulochana. K vs The Divisional Manager on 4 June, 2025

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioners in O.P.(MV) No.592/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Pathanamthitta, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 24/06/2019.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioners, on 06/02/2016 at about 08:45 a.m., while the deceased was walking through the K.P. road after parking his car at Pathanapuram taxi stand, motorcycle bearing registration no.KL25F7633 ridden by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down 2025:KER:39118 MACA NO. 449 OF 2020 as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
Though the deceased was immediately taken to the hospital, he succumbed to the injuries sustained.
A sum of 40,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/rider and the second respondent/owner filed a joint written statement contending that the incident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
The age, occupation and income of the deceased were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
4. The third respondent/insurer admitted the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
The age, occupation and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed was quite excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A10 were marked on the side of the claim petitioners.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the 2025:KER:39118 MACA NO. 449 OF 2020 respondents.

6. The Tribunal on a consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/rider of the motorcycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 12,98,425/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, claim petitioners have come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

sentences.text: 8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioners that when the incident occurred on 06/02/2016, the 2025:KER:39118 MACA NO. 449 OF 2020 deceased was the owner-cum-driver of a taxi.
It was alleged that the deceased was earning an amount of 40,000/- per month.
But the Tribunal, ignoring all the documentary evidence produced, fixed the notional income at 12,000/-, which is on the lower side.

The learned counsel draws my attention to the dictum of the Apex Court in Manusha Sreekumar v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2022) 17 SCC 321: AIR 2022 SC 5161, and submits that the amount may be appropriately enhanced.

entities.text: Manusha Sreekumar v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., (2022) 17 SCC 321: AIR 2022 SC 5161
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent/insurer that in the light of the materials on record, the amount of 12,000/- fixed by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and that it does not call for any enhancement.
In the light of Exts.A6, A8 and A10 and in the light of the dictum in Manusha Sreekumar (Supra), I find that the notional income can be fixed at 15,600/- per month.
Loss of consortium

Admittedly,
the claim petitioners three in number are the 2025:KER:39118 MACA NO. 449 OF 2020 wife and two children of the deceased.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 40,000/- to the first claim petitioner towards spousal consortium.

Going by the dictums in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.
v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130:
2018 KHC 6697, United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur, AIR 2020 SC 3076: 2023 KHC 760 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Somwati, 2020 KHC 6530 : (2020) 9 SCC 644, claim petitioners 2 and 3, who are the children of the deceased, are entitled to compensation towards parental consortium of 40,000/- each.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Admittedly,
the claim petitioners three in number are the 2025:KER:39118 MACA NO. 449 OF 2020 wife and two children of the deceased.
As per the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Pranay Sethi, 2017 (5) KHC 350: (2017) 16 SCC 680, pronounced on 31/10/2017, the consortium amount is liable to be enhanced @10% every three years.
The claim petitioners 2 and 3 were not granted consortium by the Tribunal.
Hence, they are entitled to two enhancements at the rate of 10% each, that is, on 31/10/2020 and 31/10/2023.
Therefore, claim petitioners 2 and 3 will be entitled to 48,400/- each.

Therefore, compensation towards love and affection shall stand set aside.
